scope: Curated No-Gi-priority graph for simulator testing; not a comprehensive BJJ ontology. Second pass adds shared Gi/No-Gi control state without changing the 20-position/65-transition backbone.
normalization_principles: Player A perspective is encoded in each non-standing state ID.
Player B actions are explicit on transitions and may change Player A's role in the destination.
Pose, posture, handedness, and most grips are collapsed into canonical states.
Only successful transitions are modeled; attempts/counters are deferred.
All submissions terminate at a shared absorbing node; the technique and winner remain on the edge.

sources.name: Eelis/GrappleMap repository and README
sources.license: Public domain statement in repository; no SPDX identifier
sources.use_in_this_pass: No-Gi positional/transition cross-check and broad control tags only
sources.finding: The README says the project is No-Gi focused, clothes are not modeled, hand-fighting is barely modeled, and the code/data are public domain.

sources.name: IBJJF Rules Books and Videos
sources.use_in_this_pass: Authoritative link to Rule Book v6.0 and illegal-moves material
sources.finding: Used as the sport-rule anchor; the SimRoll vocabulary does not attempt to encode every competition-specific grip foul.

sources.name: IBJJF Uniform Requirements
sources.finding: The official page specifies a grippable woven Gi with collar, sleeves, pants and belt, while No-Gi attire is a rash guard and pocketless shorts/spats.

sources.name: IBJJF Absolute GP recap
sources.use_in_this_pass: Sanity-check common Gi sleeve and collar/elbow controls in live competition
sources.finding: The report explicitly describes double-sleeve control and a sweep using collar-and-elbow grips.

sources.name: IBJJF: The Most Effective Submissions in Jiu-Jitsu
sources.finding: Describes the kimura grip as a reusable control and identifies arm-and-head isolation in common submission families.

sources.name: Gracie University public foundations curriculum
sources.use_in_this_pass: Fundamental escapes, guard work, controls, back takes and submissions
sources.finding: Used only to corroborate that selected controls and techniques are fundamental, not to infer exact hand-placement requirements.

sources.name: Gracie University: Double Underhook Pass
sources.finding: Public lesson names double underhooks as the controlling connection for a closed-guard pass.

sources.name: Gracie University: Half-guard passing lesson index
sources.finding: Public description explicitly treats the bottom underhook as a sweep-enabling control that changes the available pass response.

sources.name: SimRoll Gi/No-Gi MVP normalization
sources.use_in_this_pass: Vocabulary size, reset policy, ownership model and mode classification
sources.finding: Fields marked SIMROLL are intentionally conservative modeling choices, not claims that a source mandates one exact grip.

control_vocabulary.evidence_basis: garment existence sourced; technique applicability normalized

control_vocabulary.description: One-on-one wrist connection without garment dependency.
Direct ankle connection used in basic open-guard sweeps and passing.

control_vocabulary.player_relationship: owner controls opponent leg above the ankle
control_vocabulary.description: Broad leg connection for takedowns and passes when ankle-level precision would be false.
control_vocabulary.evidence_basis: common BJJ convention plus conservative normalization

control_vocabulary.player_relationship: owner uses two arms against one opponent arm
control_vocabulary.description: Canonical two-on-one arm control, including basic arm-drag connections.
Outcome-level arm isolation for kimura, Americana, armbar, triangle and gift-wrap entries; not a specific grip shape.

control_vocabulary.player_relationship: owner's arm passes under opponent arm/torso
control_vocabulary.description: Canonical underhook; single/double and depth variants are omitted.

control_vocabulary.player_relationship: owner's arm controls over opponent arm
control_vocabulary.description: Canonical overhook/whizzer-level control without side or depth detail.
Head-and-shoulder turning pressure used by a top/controller role.
Torso-closing connection; hand-clasp type and high/low placement are omitted.

control_vocabulary.player_relationship: owner controls opponent from behind with over-under upper-body connection
control_vocabulary.description: Canonical back/turtle upper-body control; choking-arm side is omitted.
Broad head control for front-headlock and guillotine availability when head-and-arm precision is unnecessary.
control_vocabulary.evidence_basis: common BJJ convention plus broad normalization

control_vocabulary.player_relationship: owner controls opponent head plus one arm
control_vocabulary.description: Combined head/arm enclosure for arm-triangle and D'Arce families.

control_change_transitions.notes: Parameterized template; runtime validates the selected control against position allowed_controls and owner-role constraint.

Gi-only parameterized template; unavailable in No-Gi before any state mutation occurs.
Parameterized voluntary release; does not count as positional motion.
Atomic release-plus-establish template; both controls must be legal in the current mode and position.

active_control_instance.invariant: owner_player and target_player are concrete stable player IDs; top/bottom/controller roles are derived from the current position record.

transition_control_template.requirement_semantics: All requirement clauses must be satisfied; each any_of clause needs one listed control valid for the active mode.

destination_validation_order: execute transition after resolving actor/opponent to concrete players
move to destination position and assign destination roles
preserve only controls named in controls_preserved_if_valid
drop controls absent from destination allowed_controls or invalid for owner_role_constraint
drop controls incompatible with active mode; reject any No-Gi garment grip before commit
integration_model.position_compatibility_recommendation: Keep allowed_controls and common_controls on each position as small ID arrays. Keep mode flags and owner-role constraints on control vocabulary records; do not create a 20x17x2 compatibility table.
integration_model.conservative_reset_policy: Every original position-changing edge uses all_except_explicit_preserved. This deliberately loses some plausible grips to prevent impossible retention.
